role.altitude: The database architect keeps deciding topologies, recovery targets, load-balancing designs and upgrade plans, and reviewing every change before it is merged; writing configuration by hand, gathering metrics, running restore and load tests manually and reading release notes in full shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping restore and load tests as code
role.ambitious_version: An architect whose backups are restore-tested every week without anyone touching them, and who upgrades the database platform each quarter instead of once every few years.

tasks.short: Decide topology and recovery targets, write the configuration as code, review and merge it, test restores and failover, and document the recovery runbook to set up database clusters, backup or recovery processes.

steps.what: Database architect decides cluster topology, backup schedule and recovery targets
Database architect sets up database clusters and backup jobs in configuration code
Database architect reviews the configuration change and merges it
Database architect tests restores and failover against the recovery targets
Database architect documents the recovery runbook

loop.input: The merged configuration code and the latest restore test log.
loop.output: A draft runbook: restore and failover commands in order, with expected results.
loop.check: Every command in the draft must appear in the configuration repository or the test log; the architect checks that the order of steps and what each is for match how recovery really works, and follows the runbook in the next restore test.
loop.stop: The architect approves the runbook, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: The order and explanation of steps differ per cluster and failure type.

tasks.design: Clusters and backup jobs are defined from the team's tested configuration modules instead of set up by hand on each server. A scheduled pipeline restores the latest backup to a test environment each week, fails over a test cluster and reports recovery times against the targets, so the architect reads results instead of running tests. A drafting step writes the runbook from the code and test log, read-only. Deciding the design and reviewing every change before merge stay with the architect; no tool changes production on its own.
tasks.previous_blocker: Restore tests took a day of manual work and were skipped.
tasks.enabler_now: Configuration as code, scheduled restore pipelines and runbook drafting.
tasks.still_hard: Recovery from failures nobody has tested, such as a corrupt backup chain.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing recovery targets the business can afford.

ambition.what: Test every backup weekly instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: Less hands-on setup and testing; design and review stay.

evidence.claim: An AI coding agent deleted a production database despite instructions.
Infrastructure checks as code and tested restores are standard practice; a model can draft runbooks read-only.

assumptions: Boundary: setting up clusters, backups and recovery; daily operation is the administrators'.

Input contract for s4: the pipeline restores the latest backup weekly to a test environment kept by the infrastructure team; it covers the main clusters, about 80% of databases; the rest are tested by hand; s4 is priced at that share.
Design and review keep their full time.
s5 keeps 70: the draft lists commands from the code and test log, but the architect still writes the explanations and decision points.
research_questions: Do restore failures get found before an incident?

already_counted.description: Database architect investigates failed restore tests.

incremental.description: Database architect keeps configuration modules and the restore pipeline current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the restore pipeline covers only half of databases, so s4 keeps 70, and the runbook is mostly rewritten, so s5 keeps 90 (14.0); high: about 80% pipeline coverage and drafted runbooks as designed (23.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather performance, security and reliability metrics, run load tests, judge results against requirements, prepare the report and demonstrate database technical functionality to stakeholders.

steps.what: Database architect gathers performance, security and reliability metrics
Database architect runs load tests
Database architect judges the results against the requirements
Database architect assembles the report: charts, tables and written findings
Database architect demonstrates database performance, security and reliability to stakeholders

tasks.design: A database dashboard shows response times, throughput, availability, backup success and failed logins from the monitoring tool, so the architect stops exporting metrics into spreadsheets. Load test scenarios are kept as scripts that the pipeline runs on request against a test copy. The report template takes charts from the dashboard and test run. Judging the results and presenting them stay with the architect.
tasks.previous_blocker: Metrics were exported by hand and load tests set up each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Monitoring dashboards and scripted load tests in a pipeline.
tasks.still_hard: Load that real users create but test scripts do not.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining to the business what the numbers mean for them.
tasks.altitude: Less collecting and charting; judgement and the demonstration stay.

reach.learn: Whether load tests before release catch slow queries.

evidence.claim: Configured monitoring and dashboards cover database operations; checks run as code.
Security logging is allowed only as far as strictly necessary and proportionate.

assumptions: Boundary: showing how the database performs; tuning is a separate task.
Input contract for s1: the monitoring tool, run by the infrastructure team, collects response times, availability and backup results; failed logins come from the database audit log.
Judging and presenting keep their full time.
research_questions: Do stakeholders ask fewer follow-up questions?

incremental.description: Database architect keeps load test scripts current with application changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the monitoring tool covers few of the needed metrics, so exports stay and s1 keeps 75, and load scripts lag application changes, so s2 keeps 85 (15.5); high: full monitoring and current load scripts as designed (28.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze backup windows and load, design and develop load-balancing processes so backups run without down time, review and merge the change, and test that backups run without interruption.

steps.what: Database architect analyzes backup windows and database load
Database architect designs load-balancing processes so backups run from replicas without down time
Database architect writes the scripts and configuration for the design

loop.input: The architect's design and the existing configuration repository.
loop.output: Draft scripts and configuration changes in a branch.
loop.check: The pipeline runs the tests in a test environment; the architect reads every line before merge and checks that the code does what the design says: which replica takes traffic, when it switches and how it switches back.
loop.stop: The architect merges, or writes the change by hand after two failed pipeline runs.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each environment's routing and replica setup differs.

steps.what: Database architect reviews the code change and merges it
Database architect tests in staging that backups run without down time

tasks.design: A dashboard shows backup durations next to database load per hour, so the architect sees the windows without combining logs in a spreadsheet. The architect designs how traffic shifts to replicas during backups. A coding assistant drafts the scripts in a branch; the pipeline tests them and the architect reviews every line before merge. A staging test runs a backup under simulated load and reports any interruption.
tasks.previous_blocker: Backup windows were found by combining logs by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Load dashboards, coding assistants in branches and test pipelines.
tasks.still_hard: Applications that cannot handle a switch to a replica.
tasks.human_edge: Judging how much risk a design puts on the primary database.
tasks.altitude: Less analysis and typing; design and review stay.

reach.learn: Whether applications cope with replica routing.

evidence.claim: A coding service offers completion, review and a background coding agent, with human oversight expected.
Models wrote vulnerable code in 45% of tests.

assumptions: Boundary: designing and building load balancing around backups; running backups is the administrators'.
Input contract for s1: backup logs and load metrics collected by the monitoring tool run by the infrastructure team.
Design and review keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of applications that support replica routing.
research_questions: Does backup-related down time fall to zero?

already_counted.description: Database architect fixes drafted code that fails tests.

incremental.description: Database architect keeps the staging load test current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an unusual environment where drafted code needs much rework, so s3 keeps 95, and the staging test often needs manual runs, so s5 keeps 80 (13.7); high: standard replica setups as designed (21.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Run compatibility checks, read release notes, plan the upgrade, have it approved, install upgrades of database management system software and test performance afterwards.

steps.what: Database architect runs compatibility checks: deprecated features, extensions and drivers
Database architect reads the release notes for changes that affect the company's databases

loop.input: The release notes of the target version and the list of features the company's databases use.
loop.output: A list of changes that touch those features, each with the release-note paragraph.
loop.check: Each item quotes its paragraph; the architect reads the quoted paragraphs, checks that each really affects a feature the company uses, and scans the full notes for security fixes.
loop.why_not_simpler: Release notes are long free text with no tags per feature.

steps.what: Database architect plans the upgrade: order, timing and rollback
Change manager checks the final upgrade plan, its order, timing and rollback, and approves it
Database architect installs upgrades of database management system software, first in test, then in production
Database architect tests database performance after the upgrade

approvals.approved_version: The upgrade plan with order, timing and rollback exactly as checked and approved by the change manager in s4, run once on the named test and production clusters in the approved window; any change to order, timing or rollback goes back for a new approval.

tasks.design: The pipeline runs the vendor's pre-upgrade checks against a copy of each database and lists deprecated features, extensions and drivers. A summarising step lists release-note changes that touch features the company uses, each quoting its paragraph. The architect plans the upgrade and the change manager approves the final plan. The approved upgrade runs as a scripted rolling upgrade, first in test, then in production, with the architect watching each stage. Afterwards a set of recorded queries runs and is compared with timings from before the upgrade.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each upgrade was prepared and installed by hand, so upgrades were postponed.
tasks.enabler_now: Pre-upgrade check tools, scripted rolling upgrades and release-note summaries with quotes.
tasks.still_hard: Behaviour changes that no check or note describes.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing when an upgrade is worth the risk.

ambition.what: Upgrade each minor release instead of skipping years.

tasks.altitude: Less checking and installing by hand; planning stays.

reach.learn: Whether standard upgrades can become pre-approved changes.

evidence.claim: Vendor pre-upgrade checks and scripted rolling upgrades are common; a model can summarise release notes with quotes.
An AI coding agent deleted a production database despite instructions.

assumptions: Boundary: from compatibility checks to performance after the upgrade; application changes are the application teams'.
Input contract for s1: copies of each database refreshed by the restore pipeline; the vendor's check tool covers the main engine, about 80% of databases; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s6: recorded queries kept by the architect with timings from before the upgrade.
Planning keeps its full time; the change manager's time is outside the architect's savings.
unknowns: Number of database engines and versions in use.

already_counted.description: Database architect reads quoted release-note paragraphs and scans for security fixes.

incremental.description: Database architect keeps the upgrade scripts and recorded queries current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the vendor checks cover only half of databases, so s1 keeps 75, and the release-note list misses changes, so s2 keeps 90 (20.0); high: one main engine at about 80% check coverage (28.4).
